newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian executives say wage raises to stay flat-poll.
newsitem.headline: Asian executives say wage raises to stay flat-poll.

text.p: Asian business executives said they expect year-end bonuses and salary raises for next year to remain flat to lower, a poll on Tuesday said.
The survey of several hundred executives found that 59 percent expected bonuses to stay the same, and 21.3 percent said they planned to cut down the amount they give.
Only 19.7 percent of those polled said they planned to hand out bigger bonuses this year compared with last year.
Raises were also expected to be unchanged to lower with 54 percent stating that salary increments would be the same, and 25.1 percent expecting to give smaller raises this year.
The survey also found that prospects for wages in Singapore and Thailand were grim with 50 percent of executives planning to reduce the raises they award this year.
In Thailand and the Philippines, however, 50 percent said they would give out bigger raises this year.
The poll was conducted by Asian Business News and the Far Eastern Economic Review.
